name: Playrix
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Irish developer of free-to-play mobile puzzle games including Township, Fishdom, Homescapes and Gardenscapes.
capacity_detail: Revenue around USD 1.83bn in financial year 2023; valued at USD 8bn in 2021
markets: Mobile players worldwide via App Store and Google Play; studios across Europe including Serbia, Armenia and Croatia
rationale: Top-three mobile game publisher spending heavily on user acquisition; F1's young global audience suits mass-market mobile brand building.

name: Smilegate
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: South Korean game developer and publisher behind CrossFire, Lost Ark and Epic Seven, run as a corporate group.
capacity_detail: Revenue KRW 1.577 trillion in 2022 (about USD 1.2bn); KRW 1.43 trillion (USD 1.08bn) in 2021
markets: Korea, China (CrossFire), North America and Europe through Lost Ark and Epic Seven releases
rationale: Korean publisher with global PC titles; Korean rival Krafton (PUBG) already uses F1 to reach Western gamers.

name: Valve
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: American video game developer, publisher and hardware maker that runs the Steam digital distribution platform.
capacity_detail: Annual revenue of USD 5bn by 2023 per a Forbes Australia report cited on Wikipedia
markets: PC gamers worldwide through Steam; Steam Deck and other hardware sold internationally
rationale: Owns Steam and Counter-Strike; hardware launches like Steam Deck need mass-reach brand moments F1 can provide globally.

name: Savvy Games Group
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Saudi video game investment, publishing and esports holding company created by the Public Investment Fund.
capacity_detail: Video game division of Saudi Arabia's PIF; announced USD 37.8bn games investment plan (2022) and bought Scopely for USD 4.9bn
markets: Saudi Arabia plus global holdings in Scopely, ESL FACEIT Group and Asian esports; Moonton deal announced 2026
rationale: State-backed games champion building Saudi brands internationally; F1's Saudi and Gulf races fit its national gaming-hub agenda.

name: New Balance
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: American athletic footwear and apparel brand selling running, lifestyle and team sports products worldwide.
sponsorships: Kit supplier to Atalanta (2025), Bayer Leverkusen (2025), West Ham (2026), Lille (2016), Porto (2014); NBA partner; Boston Red Sox and New York Mets
markets: Sold worldwide; football kit deals across Europe, Asia, Latin America and Australia
rationale: Fast-growing sportswear challenger to Nike and adidas; F1 offers lifestyle reach where rivals Puma and adidas are already active.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: Decathlon
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: French sporting goods retailer and designer of own brands with about 1,900 stores in 82 countries.
sponsorships: Paris 2024 Olympic partner; owns Decathlon-CMA CGM cycling team; IBU biathlon World Cup; Decathlon Arena naming rights (Lille); Kipsta ball for UEFA Europa League
markets: 1,902 stores in 82 countries and regions across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas
rationale: Global sports retailer moving brand upmarket; F1 hospitality and fan reach would support its premium push internationally.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: Prime Hydration
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Sports and energy drink brand co-founded by creators Logan Paul and KSI with Congo Brands.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.2bn in 2023 (USD 250M in 2022), per Bloomberg cited on Wikipedia
sponsorships: UFC official sports drink (2023); Arsenal (2022); FC Barcelona and Bayern Munich (2023); Borussia Dortmund (2024); Juventus (2024); SL Benfica (2024-2027); NASCAR Kyle Larson (2024); WWE
markets: United States, United Kingdom and Europe; football and combat-sports partnerships in several countries
rationale: Creator-led drink brand built on sports deals; F1's Gen-Z growth matches its audience while UK sales need revival.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: Rare Beauty
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Cosmetics brand founded by Selena Gomez, sold through Sephora, Ulta Beauty and its own website.
capacity_detail: Valued at over USD 2bn in 2024 (Bloomberg, Business of Fashion); net sales above USD 400M in 12 months to Feb 2024
markets: North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East via Sephora; Ulta Beauty from February 2026
rationale: Beauty brands like ELEMIS already use F1; Rare Beauty could reach F1's growing young female fanbase globally.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: Olipop
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: American maker of prebiotic, low-sugar functional soda sold through grocery and convenience retailers.
capacity_detail: Series C USD 50M valuing the company at USD 1.85bn (February 2025); revenue USD 400M in 2024
markets: United States grocery, convenience and online retail
rationale: Challenger soda scaling against PepsiCo and Coca-Cola; F1's booming US fanbase offers national awareness in one platform.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: AG1
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Maker of AG1, a daily powdered greens supplement sold mainly by subscription direct to consumers.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 1.2bn as of January 2025; revenue about USD 600M in 2024 per Forbes
sponsorships: Official Nutrition Partner of LIV Golf's Ripper GC (2024)
markets: Direct-to-consumer subscriptions in the US and international markets; podcast and athlete-led marketing
rationale: Performance-nutrition brand with Lewis Hamilton as investor; F1 athlete storytelling fits its podcast-driven premium positioning.

name: Holland & Barrett
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: British health and wellness retailer selling vitamins, supplements and sports nutrition through over 1,300 stores.
markets: UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Belgium, China, Hong Kong, India, Saudi Arabia, Lithuania and UAE
rationale: Expanding wellness retailer in UK, Gulf and Asia; F1 races in those markets match its franchise growth.

name: Lavazza
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Italian family-owned coffee company selling packaged coffee and espresso systems in more than 90 countries.
sponsorships: Juventus official coffee (from 2020); Liverpool FC sponsor (2018); past personal F1 sponsorship of Nicholas Latifi (Williams)
markets: More than 90 countries via subsidiaries and distributors; plants in Italy, France, India and Brazil
rationale: Premium Italian brand with sports heritage and past F1 exposure; hospitality-heavy F1 paddock suits coffee sampling.
theme: Consumer brands: beauty, fashion, food & drink

name: Jagex
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: British developer and publisher of online games, best known for the long-running RuneScape franchise.
ownership: private equity: CVC Capital Partners and Haveli Investments
capacity_detail: Bought from Carlyle for GBP 910M (about USD 1.18bn) by CVC and Haveli in February 2024
markets: PC and mobile players worldwide, mainly North America and Europe
rationale: Plausible but niche: a PC-game publisher seeking new players could use F1's UK base for RuneScape brand awareness.

name: Sorare
group: Consumer health, creator and challenger consumer brands
desc: Fantasy sports game using licensed digital player cards for football, NBA and MLB competitions.
capacity_detail: Series B USD 680M (September 2021) valuing the company at USD 4.3bn
sponsorships: Licensing partnerships with LaLiga (2021), MLB (2022), NBA and NBPA (2022), Premier League (2023)
markets: Football fans in Europe and worldwide; NBA and MLB fans in North America
rationale: Licensed fantasy platform across major leagues; an F1 game licence would add a high-engagement motorsport vertical.
